admitCard.where: The CRP CSA section of ibps.in, signed in with your registration number and date of birth or password. No hard copy is posted.
admitCard.when: The official tentative calendar lists prelims for 10–11 October 2026 and mains for 27 December 2026. Mains call letters are for shortlisted candidates when IBPS enables the link; the calendar is not proof that a call letter has been released.
steps: Open ibps.in and go to the CRP CSA link for the current cycle.
Open the call letter download link and sign in with your registration number and date of birth or password.
Download the call letter and check your name, photo, roll number, exam date, shift, reporting time and centre address against your application.
Print it clearly. If any detail is wrong, write to the IBPS helpdesk at once, before exam day.
After the prelims result, download the mains call letter the same way when it opens.
carry: A printed call letter (a screenshot is not accepted)
One original photo ID as named in the call letter instructions, such as Aadhaar, PAN, passport, driving licence or voter ID
A passport-size photograph, if the call letter asks for one
Only what the call letter allows. Phones, watches and calculators are not allowed inside
admitCard.note: Your exact exam date, shift and city appear on the call letter itself.

answerKey.summary: IBPS does not publish question papers or official answer keys for the Clerk exam and runs no objection window. The result and scorecard are your first official feedback.
steps: Treat coaching-site keys as a rough estimate only, since results are based on scores normalised across shifts (equi-percentile method) and the shortlist is state-wise and category-wise.
Wait for the prelims and mains results on ibps.in rather than chasing keys.
Download your scorecard from the result link when it opens and save a copy.
answerKey.note: This is IBPS practice across the Clerk cycle, not an omission of the current notice: no response sheet, no provisional key and no challenge process is offered at any stage.

result.summary: Results are published as PDF lists on ibps.in, followed by a scorecard with the 'Process for Arriving at Scores' note. Prelims marks are never used in the final merit; the mains score alone forms it, and there is no interview.

stages.what: A qualifying screen, shortlisted state-wise and category-wise against vacancies on sectional cut-offs plus a minimum total (expected around November 2026 for CRP-XVI).
The merit list. Scores need minimum marks in each test and a minimum total, decided state-wise and category-wise. There is no interview after this.

Candidates who did not study the opted state's local language in Class 10 or above take a qualifying LLPT (reading, writing, speaking and understanding), arranged through an independent body. Failing it removes you from the process even with a merit-list rank, so a Class 10 mark-sheet or certificate in the language counts as proof.

Allotment of merit-listed candidates to the 11 participating banks against state-wise vacancies and reservation norms (expected March 2027 for CRP-XVI), valid for one year. Candidates just below the main list may be allotted from the reserve list in later rounds. The allotted bank then runs its own document verification and joining formalities.

result.scorecard: IBPS publishes scores with the 'Process for Arriving at Scores' note on ibps.in after each result stage. Scorecards stay available for a limited window, so download and save yours.
